# google_vertex_ai_agent_anomaly_detection_scope

Agent Anomaly Detection Scope in Vertex AI.


To get more information about AgentAnomalyDetectionScope, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.agentAnomalyDetectionScopes)
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs)

## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Agent Anomaly Detection Scope Basic


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_agent_anomaly_detection_scope" "agent_anomaly_detection_scope" {
  agent_anomaly_detection_scope_id = "tf-test-scope-id"
  region                           = "us-central1"
  display_name                     = "sample-scope"
  log_buckets                      = [
    "projects/my-project-name/locations/us-central1/buckets/_Default"
  ]
  observability_buckets            = [
    "projects/my-project-name/locations/us-central1/buckets/_Default"
  ]
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `log_buckets` -
  (Required)
  Customer-owned Cloud Logging bucket resource names attached to this scope.
  Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/buckets/{bucket}`.

* `observability_buckets` -
  (Required)
  Customer-owned Cloud Observability bucket resource names attached to this scope.
  Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/observationBuckets/{observation_bucket}`.

* `agent_anomaly_detection_scope_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID to use for the AgentAnomalyDetectionScope, which will become the final component of the AgentAnomalyDetectionScope's resource name.


* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  User-provided display name of the AgentAnomalyDetectionScope.

* `encryption_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Customer-managed encryption key spec for a Scope.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_encryption_spec).

* `region` -
  (Optional)
  The region of the AgentAnomalyDetectionScope. eg us-central1

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_encryption_spec"></a>The `encryption_spec` block supports:

* `kms_key_name` -
  (Optional)
  The Cloud KMS resource identifier of the customer-managed encryption key used to protect a resource.
